0. 0.1ThisIndian FOREWORD

Standard was adopted by the Indian Standards Institution on 19 October 1967, after the draft finalized by the Sewing Machines Sectional Committee had been approved by the Mechanical Engineering Division Council.

0.2 This standard covers the requirements for square sliders for oscillating rock shafts for sewing machines for household purposes and is intended to assist in regulating the quality of indigenous square sliders. This standard is one of a series of Indian Standards on sewing machines and their components. 0.3 For the purpose of deciding whether a particular requirement of this standard is complied with, the final value, observed or calculated, expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in accordof significant places retained in ance with IS : 2-1960*. The number the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value in this standard.

NOMENCLATURE FOR SQUARESLIDERS

3.1 The square sliders and the studs shall be manufactured from any of Schedule IV of suitable case-hardening steel, such as llMn2 IS : 1570-1961* with maximum phosphorus and sulphur content of 0.05 percent each, or from steel having the following chemical composition: Constituent Carbon Silicon Manganese Sulphur Phosphorus 4. HARDNESS 4.1 The sliding faces and the bearing surfaces of the main hole of the square sliders shall be case-hardened to a minimum depth of 0.5 mm to attain a hardness value within the range of 650 to 750 HV (see IS : 1501-1959-t ) 5. 7. WORKMANSHIP

AND FINISH

7.1 The main hole and the sliding faces of the square slider shall be precision ground to attain a minimum surface finish value of Ra 0.4 pm ( see IS : 3073-1967* ).
7.2 The oil hole, fine finish. the oil grooves and the stud shall be machined to a

7.3 The square sliders shall be well finished all over and shall be free from defects such as flaw, rust, burrs or inferior surface treatment. 8. MARKING

NOTE - The use of the IS1 Certification Mark is governed by the provisions of the Indian Standards Institution ( Certification Marks ) Act, and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. Presence of this mark on products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced to comply with the requirements of that standard, under a well-defined system of inspection, testing and quality control during production. This system, which is devised and supervised by IS1 and operated by the producer, has the further safeguard that the products as actually marketed are continuously checked by IS1 for conformity to the standard. Details of conditions, under which a licence for the use of the IS1 Certification Mark may be granted to manufaoturers or processors, may be obtained from the Indian Standards Institution.

9. PACKING 9.1 Each
square slider shall be given a suitable anti-rust coating or wrapped in vapour phase inhibitor paper (commonly known as VP1 paper ). The wrapped square sliders shall be securely packed in cardboard cartons in accordance with the best prevalent trade practice. Each carton shall bear the manufacturer's name or trade-mark the type and description of contents.

APP,ENDIX ( CZuuse10.1)

A

SCALE OF SAMPLING AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY A-l. SCALE OF SAMPLING A-l.1 Lot In any consignment, all the square sliders of the same type and manufactured from the same material under essentially similar conditions of manufacture shall be grouped together to constitute a lot.
A-l.2 For ascertaining the conformity of the lot to the requirements tests shall be carried out for each lot separately. of the specification, The number of square sliders to be selected at random for this purpose shall be in accordance with co1 1 and 2 of Table 3. A-l.3 If the square sliders are packed individually, in order to ensure the randomness of selection, random number tables shall be used. In case such tables are not available the following procedure may be adopted: Starting from any square slider in the lot, count them in one part order as 1, 2, 3, . . . . . . . up to r and so on, where r is the integral Each of N/n ( N being the lot size and n the sample size ). square slider thus counted shall be selected to constitute the sample. A-1.4 If the square sliders are packed in different cartons, a suitable number of cartons ( not less than 20 percent of the total in the lot subject to a minimum of 2 ) shall be chosen at random. From each of the cartons so chosen, an approximately equal number of square sliders shall be picked up from its different parts so as to obtain the required number of square sliders specified in co1 1 and 2 of Table 3. A-2. NUMBER OF TESTS AND CRITERIA FOR CONFORMITY

A-2.1 The square sliders selected according to A-I.2 and A-l.3 or A-l.4 shall be examined for dimensions ( see 5 ), tolerances ( see 6 ) and If the number of square sliders workmanship and finish ( see 7 ). failing to meet one or more of the requirements mentioned above is less than or equal to the permissible number of defectives given in co1 3 of Table 3, the lot shall be declared as conforming to the requirements of these characteristics. A-2.2 In the case of those lots which have been found satisfactory according to A-2.1, a number of square sliders equal to the sample size indicated in co1 4 of Table 3, shall be subjected to hardness test (see 4). Any square slider failing to meet the requirement for hardness shall be considered to be defective. 7
